name: beta_weighted_gabriel_graph (Gabriel graph with per-edge beta-threshold weights)

benchmarks.note: deterministic LCG scatter in the unit square at max_beta = infinity. The kernel is an O(n^2) candidate enumeration with an O(n*d) per-pair point scan and NO early break (every other point can lower the edge's beta-threshold), so cost is O(n^3*d). 50->200 (4x points) is ~62x time (~4^3) and 200->400 (2x points) is ~8x time (=2^3), tracking the cubic scaling cleanly

fixed 300-point LCG scatter, varying max_beta. A smaller cutoff lets the `beta < max_beta` test skip the smallest-tracking update sooner, so the work decreases modestly with the cutoff (inf -> 225ms, 5 -> 181ms, 1 -> 176ms). The per-pair point scan still visits every point in all regimes, so the cutoff is only a constant-factor effect, not an asymptotic one
